title: Uber launches parking service following SpotHero acquisition, with an eye on robotaxis
summary: Uber launches dedicated parking service following SpotHero acquisition to expand robotaxi strategy
detailed: Uber launched a parking reservation and payment service in 15 U.S. cities following its acquisition of SpotHero.
The service leverages SpotHero's network of 13,000 garages, lots, and valet services across more than 400 cities.
Uber plans to use these parking locations as staging and waiting areas for autonomous vehicle partners to reduce traffic congestion and deadheading.
Users can book parking directly on the Uber app homescreen using their existing wallet and enter lots via QR codes or license plate recognition.
sentences: Uber on Monday said it is launching a new service that lets customers reserve and pay for parking in major U.S. cities, about nine months after the ride-hailing company acquired parking app SpotHero.
The acquisition, announced back in February, gives Uber access to a network of 13,000 garages, lots, and valet services across more than 400 cities, the company said.
And while Uber’s initial plans will focus on human drivers, the company also plans to leverage these parking spots to help the dozens of autonomous vehicle companies it has partnered with.

Uber said the parking spots could be used as staging and waiting locations for autonomous vehicles to help reduce congestion and deadheading, which refers to the miles a vehicle travels without a paying passenger or cargo on board.
For now, the company plans to focus on commuters driving their own vehicles.

Uber said it will initially launch in 15 U.S. cities, including Atlanta, Austin, Boston, Chicago, Dallas, Denver, Los Angeles, Miami, Nashville, New York City, Philadelphia, San Diego, San Francisco, Seattle, and Washington, DC.
Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi indicated earlier this month that the company wants the app to be more relevant to commuters.
“Commute is one of our largest categories,” he said during Uber’s third-quarter earnings call.
Uber Parking can be accessed directly on the app’s homescreen.
Users can enter their destination, select the date and time they need parking, and then review options on an interactive map.
Users can filter the results to find self-parking, valet, garages, or surface lots.
Once a user has found a parking spot, they can book after entering details about their vehicle, and use the payment method in their Uber wallet.
Once they arrive at the parking spot, users will either scan a unique QR code or gain entry through license plate recognition.
Uber said users will be able to cancel their bookings for free until the start time.
